purpose: Teach: 憶測/押しつける/歩む/破る/取り戻し/引っ張り/とらわれ/奪う

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、世論の、本気で、絶対、憶測、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、感心
lines.en: Ren, the way you handled public opinion and speculation in your paper was genuinely impressive.
lines.style: Warm, attentive approval. Lean slightly forward. Voice carries genuine interest, not performance. Steady pace—each thought lands clearly. The comfort of a teacher who means what she says.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。政府が、本気で、絶対、押しつける、絶対、政策、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you so much. I really tried to examine how government policies are imposed and the deeper implications—I'm very grateful for your guidance.
lines.style: Respectful but genuine, not stiff. Slight quickening on the gratitude at the end, as if the words are spilling out. Earnest without being overwrought. Meet her eyes, don't look down.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 歴史人物が、本気で、絶対、歩む、絶対、道、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: And the way you traced the paths historical figures took—that depth of analysis was remarkable.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost conversational. Slight pause before 'paths'—she's reflecting. Voice has a quality of discovery, like she's noticing this as she speaks. Genuine and unrushed.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。約束を、本気で、絶対、破る、絶対、政治家、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I wanted to really explore how politicians broke their promises—it felt important to document that complexity carefully.
lines.style: Quiet confidence underneath. Speak a touch faster than her, keeping pace with his own thoughts. Slight emphasis on 'important'—this mattered to him. Not defensive, just clear about his intention.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 文化財を、本気で、絶対、取り戻し、絶対、た、絶対、運動、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: The way you analyzed those movements to recover cultural heritage—that was especially thoughtful.
lines.style: Genuine admiration in the voice. Slight uptick at the end—she's pleased by what she's observing in his work. Warm but measured. Like saying something she's noticed and wants to affirm.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。民衆を、本気で、絶対、引っ張り、絶対、上げた、絶対、運動家、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you. I really wanted to honor the activists who brought people together and led those movements—their work deserved that kind of careful research.
lines.style: Voice carries both appreciation and a quiet kind of reverence. Slower pace, more deliberate. Words choose themselves carefully. Respectful of the subject, grateful to her for seeing it.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 過去に、本気で、絶対、とらわれ、絶対、ない、絶対、思想、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: What struck me was how your work wasn't trapped in the past—your thinking moved beyond it with real insight.
lines.style: Reflective, almost philosophical in tone. Gentle emphasis on 'beyond'—she's offering something he might not have fully seen in himself. Warm and observant. A gift wrapped in clarity.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。植民地が、本気で、絶対、奪う、絶対、文化、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I tried to show how colonialism stripped away cultures—and to understand what was lost in that theft. Thank you for seeing that effort.
lines.style: Quieter than before, more introspective. Words come thoughtfully, with weight. Ends with genuine emotion—gratitude that she understood what he was trying to do, not just what he wrote.
